describes: A wall of stone beside a stair, a lane or a yard: its lines, panels, courses, stones, copings and heads, laid as elevations by a mason's rules before any mesh (port step 2b; reviews/lt1/port/2b/design.md, SN2, SN9, SN10). On paper at R1: every stage is planned, and R1 lays the gully's cheek walls from this file's plan params through tools/r1_elevations.py (blender/generators/masonry.py) until the stage is wired at step 2b's re-baseline. This file holds the wall's structure (its parapet, its stepped top, its heads, its panels' teeth, its footings, where the steps' ends sit in it); the stone's sizes and how each working laid it are the pack's walling table (packs/<pack>/walling.json), by the working a wall's facts name; the rules of any wall (level beds, SN10's bond, SN2's sliver and acute limits) are code's. Its L0 and L1 triangles are the walls' budget R1 re-derived from the faces that are seen (reviews/lt1/port/2b/design.md, Triangles, 23 October: 131,100 and 53,500, at the first estimate's density); the levels below them stand at the stair's ratios to L1 until step 5, and the shading figure is the stair's until R3's frame-time A/B measures the walls. The slots and layers are provisional.
frame: Each wall line is unrolled as an elevation: s along its flight from the flight's foot point (mm), z up (mm, absolute, the pack's frame). A line beside a flight is fl-<n>/<l or r>, left or right looking up the flight; its faces are the stair's and the bank's.

l1.note: 11 mm: the value R2a's wall stones and copings were built and judged with (L1 is L0 without its chamfers: 9.21 mm on the wall stones, up to 9.8 mm on the copings). R2b replaces it with the visible joint error, measured in context, keeping the mesh error only as a check (reviews/lt1/port/2b/r2a/stones/review.md, proposal 2).
